messages.subject: Estimating population level UD
parts:
Hi!
I am trying to estimate a population level UD for migratory vultures.
I have some concern regarding this:
1. Is it advisable to use the entire cycle's data (breeding, migration, wintering, return migration) for the estimation of the UD?
2. If not, then how can I group the data for different activities (breeding, migration, wintering, return migration) apart from visual inspection?

Kindly, help me in this.
Sincerely Yours,
Dibyendu
Wildlife Institute of India

messages.author: 894c05e4b79951bb
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Estimating population level UD
parts:
Hi Dibyendu,

There are several ways people have classified movement behaviors. I have done this with elk GPS collar data in Wyoming using a combination of a couple methods. 

I first used net square displacement (nsd() function in the amt package) to determine migratory start and end dates for both spring migration and fall migration. Because you only want to use periods of range residency to run through akde() and pkde(), nsd() can help you figure out what GPS data to not run through.

Then I used a spatiotemporal segmentation method to further check the results of the nsd() dates. I used the package segclus2D (you can read more about it here: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/1365-2656.13105 ).

I’m sure there are other ways people have classified movement behavior- but these two have worked well for me. I also visually inspected the results of nsd() and segclus2d(), to triple check. Especially because the elk I study don’t always have straightforward migratory and range resident periods.

Hope this helps!
Avery

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Estimating population level UD
parts:
Hi Dibyendu,

You do want to segment the data if the autocorrelation structure of the different behaviors differs greatly, because the current models in the package are stationary. Afterwards, you can always re-combine the different UDs with mean().

Apart from visual inspection, I've heard good things about segclus2d, which Avery suggested.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: d12379035be5c6f9
messages.subject: Re: Estimating population level UD
parts:
Hi Dibyendu,
I did something similar with New World Vultures. I used migration mapper (https://migrationinitiative.org/content/migration-mapper, https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13976) to identify outbound and return migrations. Migration mapper uses a NSD to visualize and help you to identify the seasons. This is the same analysis that Avery mentioned. Migration mapper has a very friendly user interface and it returns a table with the start and end dates of each season. It also returns shapefiles with animal fixes classified for each season. While processing the data in migration mapper you can add additional information on behavior to each individual. Migration mapper now integrates ctmm.

My $0.02, hope it helps. All the best,

Adrian
